title: Sea-floor spreading and the plate tectonics revolution
summary: In 1963 the British geologists Fred Vine and Drummond Matthews, and also Lawrence Morley of the Canadian Geological Survey, proposed that zebra-stripe magnetic patterns on the ocean floor came from repeated reversals of Earth's magnetic field. Vine and Matthews's paper appeared in Nature on 7 September. Comparing the stripes with dated reversals became a clinching argument for seafloor spreading, a major advance towards plate-tectonics theory.

uncertainty.note: The date is the publication of Vine and Matthews's paper in Nature.

as_recorded.value: Published: 07 September 1963 Magnetic Anomalies Over Oceanic Ridges F. J. VINE 1 & D. H. MATTHEWS 1 Nature volume 199, pages 947–949 (1963)

In 1963, they hypothesized that the magnetic striping was produced by repeated reversals of the Earth's magnetic field, not as earlier thought, by changes in intensity of the magnetic field or by other causes.
